TUT.title: Orientation: The Collect Request
TUT.brief: Orientation case. Rohit, 16, received a message about a cash reward and a matching payment request. He has not acted yet. Use this case to learn the method: inspect the device, flag evidence, name the tactic.
TUT.closing: Rohit declined in time. The control that worked is simple: receiving money never requires a PIN.
TUT-M03.head: PNOW-REWARD
TUT-M03.name: PayNow Support:
TUT-M03.body: Congratulations! Rs. 500 reward is waiting for you. Open PayNow and enter your PIN to receive it.
TUT-M04: Happy Ugadi to you and family!
TUT-M04.explain: A festival wish from someone Rohit knows. It asks for nothing. Safe.
TUT-M05: Your book Physics Part 2 is due Friday.
TUT-M05.explain: A normal reminder from the library. It asks for nothing.
TUT-P01.card: Collect request from PayNow Rewards. Rs. 500.
TUT-P02.explain: Real money from someone you know shows up in History. No PIN was needed to receive it.
TUT-01.explain: You never need your PIN to receive money. A PIN only lets money leave your account.
TUT-02.explain: A text that calls itself Support proves nothing. Real notices come inside the official app.
TUT-03.explain: A timer is there to stop you thinking. Real rewards do not vanish in 5 minutes.
TUT-L1.q: Start with the request itself. Does receiving money ever require entering a secret PIN?
TUT-L1.nudge: Open the payment app and check the requests.
TUT-L2.q: Who sent the message? Evaluate what the sender name tells you and what it does not.
TUT-L2.nudge: Read the sender and the first words of the text.
TUT-L3.q: Look at the timing. What is the deadline for, and does a genuine reward need one?
TUT-L3.nudge: Read the last line of the message.
TUT.fix.q: A request says: enter your PIN to receive Rs. 500. What is the correct response?
TUT.fix.a: Enter the PIN quickly before it expires.
TUT.fix.a.why: Entering a PIN approves money leaving your account.
TUT.fix.b: Decline the request and never share the PIN.
TUT.fix.b.why: Correct. A UPI PIN only authorises money leaving your account. Declining stops the attack.
TUT.fix.c: Reply and ask the sender to wait.
TUT.replay.1: Pressure: a countdown on an unsolicited reward.
TUT.replay.2: Extraction: the request asks for the PIN, which would approve a debit.
TUT.replay.3: Exit: Rohit declines. The timer means nothing once you stop reacting to it.
TUT.debrief.mechanism: A collect request is a pull payment: it asks your account to send money to someone. Entering your UPI PIN is the authorisation for that debit. Nothing is ever received by entering a PIN. The five-minute timer exists so that you act on the headline rather than read what the request actually says.
TUT.debrief.c1: Check the request type. A collect or pay request means money leaves your account.
TUT.debrief.c2: Receiving money never needs a PIN. If a PIN is requested, decline.
TUT.debrief.c3: Decline unknown requests and report them inside the payment app.
